title: Taking Souls
coreMove: Use visible refusal to quit to change the pressure in a shared ordeal.
sourcePressure: The source is BUD/S and Hell Week: exhaustion, public exposure, boat crews, group pressure, and taking souls as psychological edge through relentless effort, not cruelty.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not turn taking souls into bullying, sadism, or solo domination.

hook: Take their soul before they take yours
tryThisNow: Refuse to quit for one minute

exampleSpecs.domain: storm-damaged marina salvage crew hauling soaked dock sections
exampleSpecs.audience: a new crew member watching the foreman and the tide at the same time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the crew folds before the tide window closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: as the strongest worker groans and slows, the smallest crew member silently shoulders the next dock plank and walks first into the waist-deep water
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a splintered dock plank slick with brackish mud

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital disaster drill moving patients down dead elevators
exampleSpecs.audience: a transport team under observation by skeptical senior staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fatigue spreads through the drill and proves the unit unready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the team pauses at the fourth stairwell landing, one orderly regrips the evacuation sled straps and starts the next descent without waiting for permission
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an evacuation sled wedged against a stairwell door

exampleSpecs.domain: rowing club dawn seat race against a favored crew
exampleSpecs.audience: an underdog boat that can feel the other shell waiting for it to fade
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the favored crew relaxes into victory or starts questioning itself
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coxswain calls for a power ten after the blades are already ragged, and the underdog boat holds pace until the favorite's stroke rate breaks first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet oar blade feathering under gray dawn

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse freezer inventory during a broken loading schedule
exampleSpecs.audience: a night crew working beside a rival shift that expects them to miss count
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the rival shift's certainty becomes the crew's excuse
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead worker wipes ice from the scanner, calls the next pallet number, and keeps the count moving until the rival supervisor stops joking
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a barcode scanner crusted with freezer frost

exampleSpecs.domain: wildland trail crew clearing blowdowns for a medical evacuation route
exampleSpecs.audience: a mixed crew with one member close to quitting
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the route opens before the rescue team needs it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: instead of arguing, the crew lead takes the heavy saw fuel can, steps over the next trunk, and says only the next cut
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a saw fuel can dented against a fallen cedar

exampleSpecs.domain: competitive debate team elimination round prep under sleep loss
exampleSpecs.audience: a team whose rival expects them to fold after three late nights
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fatigue makes them sloppy before the decisive round
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain erases the complaint list, posts the next evidence block, and starts cross-exam drills while the rival room can still hear them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an evidence tub with tabs bent from overnight use

skillTargets: identify psychological edge created by visible effort
choose a beat that changes group morale
analyze when effort becomes theater instead of leverage

tryThisNowSpec: In the next shared hard task, pick one visible next action that answers the room's doubt without a speech, then do it first.
